articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Meerut (UP): A 55-year-old woman, Kamlesh, died after a bullock cart accident in Kinauni village under Rohta police station. CCTV footage shows the bull suddenly panicking as she entered the village.

body.html:
Meerut (UP): A 55-year-old woman, Kamlesh, died after a bullock cart accident in Kinauni village under Rohta police station. CCTV footage shows the bull suddenly panicking as she entered the village. While trying to control it, she was trapped between the cart and a wall, sustaining severe injuries.

Villagers rushed her to the hospital, where she was declared dead. Kamlesh had been managing the farm with her two sons since her husband’s death five years ago, and was the family’s primary earning member.

articles.title: Outstation Cab Driver Brutally Attacked in Lonavala; Police Detain Accused
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Tension flared in Lonavala after a violent confrontation between local cab operators and outstation drivers, triggering public anger on social media. The incident came to light when a video showing a man assaulting a cab driver and smashing his vehicle with a stone went viral.

body.html:
Tension flared in Lonavala after a violent confrontation between local cab operators and outstation drivers, triggering public anger on social media. The incident came to light when a video showing a man assaulting a cab driver and smashing his vehicle with a stone went viral.

The Lonavala Rural Police have detained the accused, identified as Sonya Gupta, who was captured on camera vandalising the cab and repeatedly hitting the driver. In the video, the driver is heard pleading, “Dada, I just went to have breakfast. Please don’t break the car.” Despite this, Gupta continues to damage the vehicle’s front and rear windshields.

According to Police Inspector Dinesh Tayde, “The video is circulating on social media. We have detained Sonya Gupta and further investigation is underway.”

Local drivers allege that such attacks on outstation cab operators are not new. They claim that similar incidents have occurred earlier and accuse some MLAs of providing protection to those involved. Outstation drivers have demanded stronger action, calling the repeated assaults a result of growing impunity.

The Lonavala Rural Police have launched a detailed inquiry into the latest incident as well as past complaints of harassment and political shielding.

articles.title: UP Cop’s Illicit Affair Turns Fatal: Sub-Inspector Arrested for Brutal Murder of Married Lover
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: A shocking crime in Hamirpur district, Uttar Pradesh, has raised serious questions about the conduct of the UP Police, after a serving sub-inspector was arrested for the murder of his girlfriend. The sensational case was solved within two days.

body.html:
A shocking crime in Hamirpur district, Uttar Pradesh, has raised serious questions about the conduct of the UP Police, after a serving sub-inspector was arrested for the murder of his girlfriend. The sensational case was solved within two days.

According to police, SI Ankit Yadav, posted at Kabrai police station in Mahoba, killed his lover Kiran Singh, a married woman from Mahoba. He allegedly beat her to death with an iron rod, stripped the body, stuffed it in a sack and dumped it along the Maudaha–Rath road near Ramna village. Passersby spotted the corpse being torn apart by stray dogs on November 13.

Three police teams were formed and soon identified the woman as Kiran Singh. Call records revealed her connection with SI Ankit, who was arrested from his official quarters on Sunday.

Police said the two went out for a drive on November 12. An argument broke out, and the enraged officer killed her using an iron rod kept in the car. Postmortem confirmed a fractured skull and marks of strangulation.

Kiran, whose husband Vinod is a CRPF jawan, had earlier filed a dowry harassment case against him and his family. SI Ankit was the investigating officer in that case, during which he grew close to her. Kiran’s family alleges that Vinod and his relatives may have colluded with the officer to eliminate her.

Ankit Yadav, a 2023 batch SI from Rae Bareli, comes from a police family — his father is also a sub-inspector posted in Varanasi.

Police are now probing all angles, including the family’s allegations of conspiracy.

articles.title: Adopted Girl Zara, 4, Brutally Killed in Amroha? Stepmother Arrested After Shocking Post-Mortem
articles.author: The Times Patriot
articles.excerpt: Amroha: A four-year-old adopted girl, Zara, was found dead under suspicious circumstances in Mohalla Qureshi, triggering a major police investigation. Initial inspection revealed multiple bruises on her face and body.

body.html:
Amroha: A four-year-old adopted girl, Zara, was found dead under suspicious circumstances in Mohalla Qureshi, triggering a major police investigation. Initial inspection revealed multiple bruises on her face and body. Police detained her stepmother, Shaista, on suspicion of assault and murder.

Zara was adopted by handloom artisan Mohammad Islam and his late wife Saira shortly after her birth. Saira passed away five months ago, after which Islam married Shaista, a divorcee from Sambhal. The family lived in a rented house in Gali No. 2 of Mohalla Qureshi.

On Thursday morning (13 Nov 2025), Islam left for work at 8 a.m., but around 9:30 a.m., Shaista called him claiming Zara was unwell and having difficulty breathing. Islam rushed home and took the child to a private hospital, where doctors declared her dead. Noticing injury marks, Islam informed his family and the police.

Inspector Pankaj Tomar reached the spot with his team, and a forensic team collected evidence. Shaista was taken into custody for questioning. SP Amit Kumar Anand also interrogated her at the police station. Initially, the family did not lodge a complaint.

A panel of doctors later conducted the post-mortem, which revealed over 12 injury marks and confirmed that Zara had been brutally beaten and strangled. Following the report, Islam filed a complaint, after which police registered a murder case against Shaista. She was arrested, produced in court, and sent to jail. During interrogation, she confessed to the crime.

According to police, Shaista allegedly beat Zara after she dirtied her clothes while playing and then strangled her to death. To hide the crime, she told Islam that the child was unwell and falsely claimed the girl had fallen from the stairs. Neighbours reportedly heard the child's screams but avoided speaking to the police.

Zara’s biological parents, Qayyum and Naima of Panju Sarai, who had legally given her up for adoption, were devastated after learning of her murder. Islam too is shattered, having lost his first wife and adopted daughter within six months.
